UFC heads to the U.A.E. for UFC 333, headlined by a pair of really intriguing and evenly matched title fights. In the main event, Alexander Volkanovski will look to continue his second reign as featherweight champion when he faces top contender Movsar Evloev. Evloev brings a perfect 20-0 professional record to the Octagon against a legend who has looked ageless in his second run with the title.Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 333 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! The rest of the main card has more evenly matched fights that could provide some answers for key divisions as the end of the year approaches. title: 2026 World Series: Brandon Woodruff makes Brewers' roster after long injury layoff - CBS Sports
description: Woodruff, who debuted with Milwaukee in 2017, hasn't pitched since July 4 due to a shoulder issue
body:
Woodruff, who debuted with Milwaukee in 2017, hasn't pitched since July 4 due to a shoulder issue
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Right-hander Brandon Woodruff, the longest-tenured player on the Milwaukee Brewers, has made the club's World Series roster. Woodruff has not pitched in an MLB game since July 4 due to what was initially considered a severe shoulder injury, though he showed enough improvement in August to begin a throwing program. Game 1 of the Fall Classic between the Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays is set for Friday night in Milwaukee. "We know who the kid is. We know his -- that it's not going to be too much for him. This is what this kid's all about. He's been around here for ten years or whatever, and we've understood it. We feel like there's a window where he can help us," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said on Friday."That was the whole decision. This isn't a, 'wow, we love Woody, he's great for the organization' -- because he already said to us, I don't want to be a sympathy pick. I want to be a pick because I can help the team. Then you go through all the things and say, can he help us? The answer is yes, he can definitely help us."
        
            
                Three biggest questions for World Series Game 1 as Brewers and Rays kick off 2026 Fall Classic
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Now 33, Woodruff made nine effective starts prior to the shoulder injury this season. He missed the entire 2024 season after having surgery on his shoulder, returned to make 12 starts in 2025, and then was on the Opening Day roster this year. It was initially feared that Woodruff would require another surgery in July. That ultimately was not the case.
Murphy acknowledged the roster rules would play a role in carrying Woodruff on the World Series roster. Injured players can be replaced on the postseason roster if they suffer a new injury. By rule, the Brewers would not be able to replace Woodruff if he suffers a setback and re-injures his shoulder. They're gambling that his shoulder will hold up.
"I didn't want this to be a charity pick," Woodruff said on Friday. "That was important to me. I wanted to feel like I could -- I wanted to be on the roster because I felt like I could help win. So I did not want this to be part of the decision."Woodruff said he met with Murphy and president of baseball operations Matt Arnold on Thursday before the final decision was made.
"It didn't really hit me," he said of the call from Murphy to tell him he'd made the roster. "I was kind of like thank you for the opportunity and, basically, let's go win this thing. That was pretty much the extent of the conversation. It was like they've got work to do, I've got a job to do to mentally prepare, and I just thanked them. That was pretty much it, yeah."During his nine starts this season, Woodruff pitched to a 2.98 ERA with 47 strikeouts and only nine unintentional walks in 45 ⅓ innings. At times, his fastball clocked as high as 96.0 mph. There were also times when he sat in the upper 80s. The movement traits on his fastball remain terrific, allowing it to play at reduced velocity.It is unknown how the Brewers intend to use Woodruff, though it seems likely he won't be much more than a one- or two-inning option given the injury and long layoff. Truth be told, he may only see the mound in a blowout. Regardless, the Brewers consider him healthy enough to contribute in some capacity. Woodruff, who has spent his entire MLB career with the Brewers after debuting in 2017, replaced right-hander Chad Patrick on the roster. Patrick was on the NLDS and NLCS rosters, but did not pitch.
Game 1 of the World Series will be played Friday night at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Both the Brewers and Rays are seeking their first-ever championship. National League Cy Young favorite Jacob Misiorowski will start for the Brewers, while the Rays counter with Nick Martinez -- a somewhat unexpected choice.

title: Lamar Jackson injury update: Ravens QB hopeful to return vs. Bengals in Week 7 - CBS Sports
description: Baltimore's offense could be back at full strength soon as Jackson progresses toward a possible return against Ci
body:
Baltimore's offense could be back at full strength soon as Jackson progresses toward a possible return against Cincinnati
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Baltimore Ravens could be on the verge of getting their starting quarterback back in the lineup. Lamar Jackson, who has missed the last two-and-a-half games due to an ankle injury, said on Friday that he is hopeful to play on Sunday against the division rival Cincinnati Bengals."Right now, I'm heading in the right direction," Jackson said. "I can't call it right now. I've still got a little grace period. So, we'll see man. Hopefully, but I feel like I'm heading in the right direction right now."Ravens coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson got a "pretty good amount of work in" during Friday's practice after he was limited on Wednesday and Thursday, but stated that the team is "still working through" whether or not Jackson will play on Sunday.For his part, Jackson said the Ravens' medical staff told him he is dealing with a high ankle sprain, per The Athletic, which he seemingly sustained on the final play of the first half of the Ravens' victory over the Tennessee Titans back in Week 4. Jackson has been described as "day-to-day" since the injury, but this week was the first time he has participated in practice since going down.
He said on Friday that he doesn't have to be 100% healthy to play, but he doesn't want to be a "statue" on the field, via The Athletic. Jackson also relayed that the decision to play through multiple injuries that limited his mobility last season was "dumb, a little bit."Jackson's rushing ability was severely limited last year, as he averaged a career-low 5.2 rushing attempts and 26.8 rushing yards per game. He had previously averaged at least 51.3 yards per game in every full season as a starter. He's averaging 36.0 yards per game so far this year, but he did leave one of those games at halftime.If Jackson is again unable to start against Cincinnati, Tyler Huntley would once again take his place under center. Huntley has gone 1-1 in his two starts, and he's 51 of 72 for 429 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions so far. He's also run 15 times for 64 yards and a touchdown. The Ravens managed 30 points in their overtime victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5, but slumped to just 10 points in their loss to the Cleveland Browns last week. 
The offense has looked electric with Jackson under center in new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's scheme, but we have rarely seen it at full strength so far this year. Not only has Jackson missed two-plus games, but Zay Flowers also missed a game-and-a-half and was limited to just 33% of the snaps in another. If they can get fully healthy, the Ravens could take off offensively. But that all depends on Jackson's ankle.

schema.headline: Lamar Jackson injury update: Ravens QB hopeful to return vs. Bengals in Week 7 - CBS Sports

title: Cam Skattebo reacts to Giants benching and Najee Harris release before Texans game - CBS Sports
description: After being effectively benched and watching New York release Najee Harris days later, Skattebo acknowledged his
body:
After being effectively benched and watching New York release Najee Harris days later, Skattebo acknowledged his situation
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The New York Giants running back room has everyone's attention following an essential benching of their star player and cutting another after he criticized the run game.Cam Skattebo leads the Giants in rushing yards with 294 yards on 81 carries, but in last week's 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints, he wasn't given a single rushing attempt. It marked the first time in his two-year NFL career that he didn't touch the ball once in a game he played in. His limited snaps and lack of opportunities were a response to his costly fumble during overtime in the team's Week 5 27-27 tie against the Washington Commanders. The running back room also saw the departure of Najee Harris, whom the Giants cut days after he started in place of Skattebo. Harris drew headlines for his criticism of the New York run game, expressing confusion over the game plan. Harris finished his short Giants tenure with 31 rushing attempts for 99 yards in five games."Nobody's safe, it's as simple as that," Skattebo said on Friday. "And I think when we go on the field, and we perform, if we're not performing, we understand there's a possibility of not being here. And if I don't perform, I know there's a possibility of me not being here."  Skattebo seemed to take what was essentially a soft benching well, saying he can learn from it. 
"I got taught a lesson," he said. "I don't know if that's from them or from myself. I had to kind of step back and look at it and figure out why. Why I was doing the things I was doing, what was happening. Came to practice, worked on those things, corrected them. Ready to go back out there and play ball."This was similar to his locker-room commentary after Sunday's game."I got punished for what I did [in last week's tie]," Skattebo said. "I understand it. I gotta be ready when coach calls my name and that wasn't today... I didn't expect to have zero [touches], but I was expecting to not play as much like I did."
The Giants are in Houston to face the Texans on Sunday.

title: Knicks reportedly duped employees with championship ring email that was actually a phishing test - CBS Sports
description: Knicks coaches, meanwhile, received empty ring boxes during the opening-night ceremony this week
body:
Knicks coaches, meanwhile, received empty ring boxes during the opening-night ceremony this week
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:45 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The New York Knicks went on one of the more euphoric championships in NBA history earlier this year. It was an unforgettable playoff run that ended a 53-year title drought. But a lot of the news surrounding the team since then has had a different tone.Whether it's been owner James Dolan's hard-line stance against going into the second apron costing the team key reserve Mitchell Robinson or contentious extension negotiations with multiple starters getting tabled before the season, the vibes surrounding New York's championship defense are significantly more dour than they were even a few months ago.And, on Thursday, The Athletic reported that the issues haven't just been confined to the roster. While Knicks players received their championship rings on Tuesday before their season-opening loss to the Philadelphia 76ers, the rest of the organization appears to still be waiting. Knicks assistant coaches reportedly did not receive their rings on Tuesday night despite being handed (apparently empty) boxes during the ring ceremony. While the assistants' reactions to not getting their rings reportedly ranged "from genuine anger to annoyance," The Athletic noted that not all assistant coaching staffs, including last year's Oklahoma City Thunder, get their rings on opening night.
However, in an atypical move by NBA standards, many longtime Madison Square Garden employees reportedly will not receive a championship ring at all. While the most expensive and ornate championship rings tend to be reserved for the players, most employees of NBA teams receive less expensive rings when their team wins a title. The New York Post reported Friday that the plan is to distribute a total of 275 championship rings "to players, coaches, employees and other members of the Knicks family, worth more than $3.7 million."And yet, as a means of testing the organization's cybersecurity, Madison Square Garden employees received an email in September asking them to reserve their preferred ring style. The email, however, was reportedly a phishing test. Employees who clicked on the link were forced to attend a mandatory cybersecurity class "to help satisfy some of Dolan's growing cybersecurity concerns." It is not clear how many of the employees who received this email will eventually be awarded a championship ring.On Friday, an MSG spokesperson called the decision "an unfortunate mistake" in a statement to the New York Post:
"The company had previously sent out an email to its corporate team as a simulation of a phishing attack designed to strengthen our security against hackers. MSG was recently hacked and extorted using an employee login and password obtained through a similar phishing attack. Using the rings as a lure to gain employees attention was an unfortunate mistake."The Knicks kicked off their title defense with a loss to LeBron James and the 76ers, and while the season is only just getting underway, much of the goodwill that followed last spring's magical run appears to have dissipated. Though off-court controversies have been minimal since Leon Rose was hired to run the team, the Knicks are seemingly courting a pretty avoidable one in how they've handled the dispersal of their championship rings.

schema.headline: Knicks reportedly duped employees with championship ring email that was actually a phishing test - CBS Sports

title: Should Seahawks trade for Jonathan Taylor? Pros, cons for reigning champions to add Colts superstar - CBS Sports
description: Less than nine months ago, Kenneth Walker III powered the Seahawks to a Super Bowl LX victory with 161 yards from scrimmage, won Super B
body:
Less than nine months ago, Kenneth Walker III powered the Seahawks to a Super Bowl LX victory with 161 yards from scrimmage, won Super Bowl MVP ... and then left Seattle, becoming the first Super Bowl MVP to change teams the ensuing offseason in over two decades.Walker took Seattle's entire running game with him. While he leads the NFL in rushing yards and yards per carry in Kansas City, the Seattle running game is wallowing among the league's worst. With Zach Charbonnet missing the first six weeks of the season, Seattle has rotated through runners -- first-round rookie Jadarian Price leading the way at first before landing on IR with a chest injury, then Emanuel Wilson after Price's injury, with a sprinkling of George Holani as a change-of-pace/third-down/pass-catching option.None have produced. Not only that, but all three have committed the cardinal sin: turning the ball over. Price lost fumbles in Week 2 and Week 3. Wilson and Holani both lost fumbles in Week 5, gifting the 49ers 14 points. Holani's, with Seattle simply trying to run out the first-half clock, was particularly awful, and Mike Macdonald could hardly believe his eyes.
The Seahawks rank last in rushing expected points added, largely due to an enormous number of fumbles. But even excluding fumbles, Seattle ranks 27th in rushing success rate, a measure of down-to-down efficiency. Seattle's 34 runs of 0 or negative yards are tied for eighth-most.
Charbonnet will help -- he has zero fumbles in his NFL career,  he is a good pass catcher and protector, and he has 21 touchdowns over the past two seasons -- but to lean on him heavily would be unwise. It's not just because of the injury, but also because he's never been a bell cow. He split backfield duties with Walker each of the last three years. His career high in touches per game is 12.8, set last year. Furthermore, Charbonnet simply doesn't provide the explosive element Walker did.Someone who does provide an explosive element and bell cow capability is Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. He has topped 1,500 yards from scrimmage each of his last three healthy years, and last year he had 1,963, as well as 20 total touchdowns. With the Colts firing GM Chris Ballard earlier this week, Indianapolis could be looking to sell.NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said if Taylor is available, he'll 1) have many potential suitors and 2) have a high price. Rapoport also pointed out the Colts' interim GM, Ed Dodds, came up through Seattle (he was with the team from 2007-16) and has strong connections there.

        
            
                Jonathan Taylor mock trades: How Giants, Bengals could target Colts star RB after Chris Ballard's firing
                
                    Zachary Pereles                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Does the shoe fit for Taylor and the Seahawks? Does it even make sense to see if it does? Here are the reasons for and against Seattle making the move.Why the Seahawks should trade for Jonathan TaylorTaylor, 27, is still a stud. He's maybe not quite as studly this year -- many of his rate numbers are down -- but there might be reasons for that.The Colts' offense is a mess. Like the Seahawks, they are turning the ball over a ton. Unlike the Seahawks, they have no answer outside the run game. Alec Pierce has appeared in two games due to an ankle injury that required surgery this offseason and then got re-aggravated. This was a thin receiver group before Pierce, but now it has no deep threat. Tyler Warren has also missed time.
All of this is to say things are stacked against Taylor. He is currently averaging 1.25 yards before contact per rush, which would be the lowest number of his career. Taylor's 2.79 yards per attempt are down from last year, but not a career-worst. His tackle avoidance rate is also down, but it's harder to make people miss when there aren't as many clear running lanes to the second level.Taylor showed he can still be a major factor. He has had 120+ yards from scrimmage in three of six games this season. He has also scored multiple touchdowns in three of those six games. His numbers may be down -- 4.0 yards per carry -- but this is a certified bell cow. He'd take the pressure off the turnover-prone Sam Darnold and would be able to carry the offense by himself for stretches if needed. A relentless run game plus a relentless, dominant defense sounds like a pretty good combination.If the Seahawks want to put their best foot forward in defending their title, they have to find answers in the run game. First-year offensive coordinator Brian Fleury was in San Francisco when the 49ers acquired Christian McCaffrey and elevated him into superstar status. He'd know how to elevate Taylor.
Plus, the Seahawks have crushed their in-season trades recently: Rashid Shaheed last year, Ernest Jones the year before, and Leonard Williams the year before that. Taylor could be the next game changer.Why the Seahawks shouldn't trade for Jonathan TaylorAt 3-3, Seattle is far from out of it, especially in an NFC that doesn't look very deep beyond the loaded NFC North. Charbonnet's return will provide far more stability to a running game that needs it, and Macdonald anticipates a "sooner rather than later return" for Price after the Week 7 game against the Chiefs.Seattle just invested a first-round pick in Price, too. He looked very good in the season opener against the Patriots and was solid against the Cardinals in Week 2, aside from the fumble. Another fumble in Week 3 against the Commanders plus an injury is a tough combination, but his return should provide a boost in the explosives department.
Taylor's dip in efficiency this year doesn't tell the whole story by itself, but it's not a good sign, either. He led the NFL in touches in 2025, his most since 2021. He has missed at least three games due to injury in three of the last four seasons. Yes, he's only 27, but the wear and tear on his body is considerable.Through six games, Taylor doesn't have a single carry of 25+ yards; he had seven last year and eight the year before. He isn't producing big plays at the rate he was even a year ago. NFL Next Gen Stats has him averaging -0.16 yards over expected per rush, the first time ever he's been on the negative side of that metric. In fact, he's usually been one of the best. That downward trend is concerning, and he's signed with a significant salary cap hit through 2028.He is still a very, very good player. But an elite one? Potentially not. And if he costs what an elite player costs -- not just with trade compensation, but actually payment into the future -- the Seahawks should pass. Just because they've had success in recent trades doesn't make Taylor the right one.
Final verdictThe Seahawks should not trade for Jonathan Taylor, and it's not just because Taylor might not be the player he once was, or because the Seahawks have two players at his position coming back.The biggest reason to not make a trade is Seattle has bigger issues offensively. The line is a mess, ranking 23rd in PFF's pass-blocking grades, 23rd in ESPN's pass-block win rate, and 25th in ESPN's run-block win rate. Macdonald acknowledged the issues up front after a Week 6 loss to the Broncos, saying "the quarterback is getting hit way too much ... everybody sees that."Taylor would help -- there's no doubt about that -- but what would help much more is Taylor's teammate Quenton Nelson. A stalwart guard for the last nine seasons in Indianapolis, Nelson is still playing at a very high level. Could he come in at left guard and move Grey Zabel to right guard to fortify the interior?
If it's not Nelson, it could be another guard or a center. Seattle needs more up front than it does in its backfield, and finding a cost-effective solution there will be much smarter than hoping one talented back can lift up an offensive ecosystem currently being dragged down by its blocking.

schema.headline: Should Seahawks trade for Jonathan Taylor? Pros, cons for reigning champions to add Colts superstar - CBS Sports

title: Bears' Cole Kmet likely facing season-ending knee injury after being carted off - CBS Sports
description: Chicago's longest-tenured player suffered a likely season-ending knee injury against New England
body:
Chicago's longest-tenured player suffered a likely season-ending knee injury against New England
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Chicago Bears earned a 30-24 victory over the New England Patriots, but they also lost a notable player on offense, as tight end Cole Kmet was carted off the field in the fourth quarter after suffering a knee injury. He's believed to have suffered a serious, likely season-ending knee injury and will be placed on injured reserve, according to ESPN.Kmet caught a Caleb Williams pass in the right flat before turning upfield and getting hit by Robert Spillane and Christian Gonzalez. When he went down, the veteran pass-catcher immediately grabbed at his right knee. Kmet caught 10 passes for 87 yards and one touchdown this season. The former No. 43 overall pick out of Notre Dame is the longest-tenured Bear on the roster and one of the team's leaders. Williams told reporters he'll be there for Kmet every step of the way as he begins his recovery. "It was tough. Obviously, I don't know exactly what it is, but getting carted off is never good. You're at least going to miss some time. I don't have the words to describe what Cole is to me, what Cole is to this team, to this organization. He's the longest-tenured Bear, I believe," Williams said. "He's been through it and it's challenging, it's tough, and I'll be right there with him through every step of whatever the injury is. Cole's been there for me every step of the way, through the first year, through the second year, and now through this year. So I could only do the same for him."
Kmet's injury means more attention for Colston Loveland, who saw a season-high 12 targets vs. New England, catching seven of them for 69 yards and a touchdown. Loveland has now caught touchdowns in back-to-back games after failing to find the end zone through the first five games of the season. The only other tight end currently on the active roster is rookie Sam Roush, who was selected in the third round this year out of Stanford. He's caught three passes for 33 yards so far this season, although he was projected as more of a "blocking tight end" as a prospect. Chicago has Qadir Ismail and Stephen Carlson on its practice squad as well. 
Up next for the Bears are the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks in Seattle on "Monday Night Football" Nov. 2.

schema.headline: Bears' Cole Kmet likely facing season-ending knee injury after being carted off - CBS Sports

title: Jesse Legree returning to Oregon State in 2027: Nation's leading receiver remains loyal to Beavers - CBS Sports
description: A midseason All-American with 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns, the breakout freshman delivers a massive statement f
body:
A midseason All-American with 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns, the breakout freshman delivers a massive statement for the Beavers by bypassing the transfer portal
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Jesse Legree – the nation's most exciting freshman and a midseason CBS Sports All-America selection – announced to the world Friday from his home gym in Baltimore, Maryland, that he will be returning to Oregon State for his sophomore season. Legree made the announcement and re-signed with the Beavers live on CBS Sports HQ. Legree's intent during the bye week was to put to rest doubts about his future and quiet portal whispers that had already begun as scouting departments around the country, beginning to devise their 2027 roster-building plans, took full notice of the 5-foot-9 Legree's exploits in Corvallis: 46 receptions and a nation-leading 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns. "I, here, will be signing to Oregon State Beavers for the 2027 to 2028 season," Legree said. "It's always some kids' dream to live out on signing day, and unfortunately, I wasn't able to have mine last year. And to be able to have one this year for this contract is great."The signing day Legree never truly hadLast December, he watched his teammates at St. Frances Academy in Baltimore sign with the likes of Alabama and Auburn. Legree was an unheralded three-star prospect with few high-level offers and no signing day home, at least during the school's morning celebrations. Legree grew up a basketball player and played defensive back his first three years of high school football. 
He joked with CBS Sports in early October that he "barely knew Oregon was a state." But newly minted Beavers general manager Eron Hodges had seen Legree while he and new OSU coach JaMarcus Shephard were at Alabama during the 2025 season, the byproduct of scouting and recruiting Bama signee Jireh Edwards, a teammate of Legree's at St. Frances Academy. "The day I got the job, Eron called me and said, 'Hey, watch this kid right now.' And I watched him right away, knowing that Eron was gonna come out here and be the GM with me," Shephard said. "And I was like, 'Yeah, we need to go get him. Let's get him.' And we started that process the day that I got the job, and so he was the first kid that I watched as the head football coach here at Oregon State, and he was the first person that I knew for sure we wanted on our team."Now, if I'm just being transparent, I didn't know for sure how good of a receiver he was. You know, his highlight tape has him doing a lot of returns. But I also watched some of his basketball stuff. You can see his quickness, change of direction, explosiveness, ability to track the ball, and all that stuff. And you're really just hoping that all that would translate into a receiver."
Oregon State called late in the day on the opening day of Early Signing Period, long after his teammates had signed and had their moment. His high school coach, Messay Hailemariam, received a text from Hodges that said, "he has a home with us if he wants it. We want to take him."Hailemariam remembers interrupting his team during a film session to share the news. 
This decision is about loyalty Legree has won seven straight Pac-12 Freshman of the Week awards. The only reason he won't win an eighth is that the Beavers are on a bye in Week 8. Legree leads the nation in yards (1,040) and touchdowns (14) and has been the catalyst for a prolific OSU offense that's sixth nationally in yards/play (7.32) and fifth in yards per game (527) and fourth in scoring offense (42.7 points per game). The Beavers are 5-2 and rolling as they get into the toughest part of their Pac-12 schedule (transfer QB Braden Atkinson, who will also have a decision to make about his 2027 future, has been great).
In today's college football, the moment a player at the Group of Six level begins to shine, there is an assumption that he will move on to what people assume are greener pastures. Conventional wisdom doubts that Oregon State can do what's necessary to keep him, but Legree is not a conventional player, and his relationship with Oregon State is not the conventional business transaction that is the new order of the day in college football. They took a chance on him, and he rewarded it at the commitment ceremony he never had. For Oregon State, this is a statement of intent as well. College football forgot about Corvallis. Its own in-state rival left them for the Big Ten, and the Beavers were left to pick up the pieces of the Pac-12 with Washington State. They're rising from the ashes to build something exciting, and retaining Jesee Legree is a big boost to the project.

schema.headline: Jesse Legree returning to Oregon State in 2027: Nation's leading receiver remains loyal to Beavers - CBS Sports

title: Revisiting the 2026 NFL Draft: Can Akheem Mesidor be a building block for Chargers defense? - CBS Sports
description: An 0-6 start shifts the conversation in Los Angeles to the future and which first-year contributors can serve as
body:
An 0-6 start shifts the conversation in Los Angeles to the future and which first-year contributors can serve as foundational pieces
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:25 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6 to start the season. They did not lose a sixth game last season until the regular season finale. Instead of making playoff plans, the conversation in Los Angeles centers on which leadership changes may be needed and which players are building blocks for the next iteration of Chargers football. Is Akheem Mesidor a building block on defense?Edge rusher had been a position commonly associated with Los Angeles leading up to the draft. Aside from Tuli Tuipulotu, the Chargers have leaned on Khalil Mack and Bud Dupree recently; both of whom are 33 years or older. Miami's Akheem Mesidor was expected to be the present and the future of a defense trying to find its footing in a post-Jesse Minter world. To this point, he has played 192 of a potential 367 defensive snaps. A trade involving Mack, who has played 71.4% of defensive snaps, would open the door for more playing time opposite Tuipulotu. Through six games, Mesidor has 10 pressures and 2.5 sacks. Most of his pressures and production result from playing to the whistle rather than winning quickly at the line of scrimmage. The Ontario native has brought his go-to chop-and-swipe moves off the edge from college to the pros, but he lacks an overwhelming trait that would allow him to consistently win off the line of scrimmage.  However, he does a good job setting the edge in the run game and forcing the opposition to play between the tackles.
Long-term outlookIf Tuipulotu can disrupt the pocket and move the quarterback off his spot, Mesidor could be a complementary starter who offers a solid floor in the run game and helps clean up the chaos. There is not much untapped potential, considering he is a 25-year-old who played six seasons of college football. Could they have gone in another direction? There is a negligible difference between Mesidor and other edge rushers taken after him in the first round. They could have taken the undersized R Mason Thomas or Cashius Howell if they wanted more pass rush production. Dani Dennis Sutton (Packers) is another quality player who was taken later.
His presence allows the organization to focus on other positions of need, such as cornerback, offensive line and more. Los Angeles is realizing its defensive needs may have been masked by Minter's influence.

title: Dale Brown dies at 90: LSU's all-time winningest basketball coach led Tigers to two Final Four apperances - CBS Sports
description: Brown spent 25 seasons leading LSU's basketball program and racked up 448 career wins
body:
Brown spent 25 seasons leading LSU's basketball program and racked up 448 career wins
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
Dale Brown, who won 448 games as LSU's basketball coach from 1972-1997 before he retired as the Tigers' all-time winningest coach, died Friday, the university announced. He was 90."We have lost the most loving and most loved man any of us has ever known," Brown's family said in a statement, "Dale Brown always put others first. He always led with his heart. He was always a great humanitarian before anything else. Dale long ago fell in love with Louisiana. And the people of Louisiana loved him right back. We are forever grateful for that."After stints as an assistant coach at Utah State and Washington State, Brown took the LSU job in 1972 and remained with the program for 25 seasons, winning 448 games. Brown led LSU to four SEC regular-season titles (1979, 1981, 1985 and 1991), an SEC Tournament title in 1980 and two Final Four appearances in 1981 and 1986.
Earlier this week, Brown was announced as the 2027 Wohn R. Wooden Legends of Coaching Award recipient. Brown, who was a longtime friend of the former UCLA coach, was set to receive the award this spring in Los Angeles."I will always remember Dale for his enthusiasm," Wooden once said about Brown. "There are those who say he is a put-on – they just can't believe that he can be what he professes. But I never questioned that. He amazed me because there is a lot more depth to the man. He was much more than a basketball coach."During his tenure at LSU, Brown notably coached future NBA legend Shaquille O'Neal and Chris Jackson (now Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf). Abdul-Rauf went on to be the No. 3 overall pick in the 1990 NBA Draft, while O'Neal was selected No. 1 overall two years later.Brown was inducted into the National Collegiate Basketball Hall of Fame in 2014.

title: Liv Golf 2.0: Tyrrell Hatton, Ian Poulter latest to announce departure from revamped league - CBS Sports
description: The deadline for players to commit to LIV Golf 2.0 is Oct. 25
body:
The deadline for players to commit to LIV Golf 2.0 is Oct. 25
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The list of players who will not be joining LIV Golf 2.0 is getting longer. Tyrrell Hatton and Ian Poulter headline the latest crop to announce that they will not be returning to the league. The pair of Englishmen were joined by Branden Grace, Tom McKibbin and Lucas Herbert on Friday as the deadline for player commitment to the league is Oct. 25."Wanted to confirm that I will not be a part of LIV 2.0," Hatton wrote on his Instagram story. "A big thank you to everyone for their continued support. I am excited for what the next chapter of my career holds. Looking forward to seeing you all in Abu Dhabi."Hatton has eyes on the DP World Tour playoffs, which begin in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 5-8, where he will make his first start since departing from LIV Golf. He will be joined in the field by his Legion XIII teammate and captain, Jon Rahm, who had already made it known that he wants nothing to do with the league moving forward.Rahm's lawyer stated that his client found the terms for LIV Golf 2.0 "unacceptable" before the two parties reached a separation agreement in which the Spaniard retained his name, image and likeness rights. Like Rahm, Hatton has playing privileges on the DP World Tour thanks to his previous victories on the circuit.The same will go for Poulter and the rest of the lot who can return to the DP World Tour in November. In his statement, the 12-time DP World Tour winner cited wanting to spend more time with his family, grow his YouTube channel and compete in some senior events as reasons for leaving LIV Golf and the Majesticks, which he has captained since the start.
"Ultimately, the opportunity to spend more time at home with my family, reduce international travel, focus on senior golf and have the opportunity to pursue other interests was something that I felt was right for me at this stage of my life and career," Poulter released in a statement.The DP World Tour put its foot in the ground two weeks ago when the league announced that any player who played in LIV Golf 2.0 would not be able to take up membership on the European circuit in 2027. To be eligible for the European Ryder Cup team, one must be a member of the DP World Tour.Other players who have indicated that they will no longer be playing on LIV Golf include Adrian Meronk, Louis Oosthuizen, Sergio Garcia, Abraham Ancer, Charles Howell III, Thomas Pieters and David Puig. Meanwhile, those who plan to play in the league should it get off the ground include Richard Bland, Ben Campbell, Cameron Tringale and Brendan Steele.
"This is where I want to be," Steele recently said. "This has been home to me for the last four years, it's been great. I'm happy to stay."

title: UFC 333: Petr Yan hopes to motivate others with his career comeback story - CBS Sports
description: Yan was counted out by many after a dramatic losing skid, but he silenced those doubters after regaining his bant
body:
Yan was counted out by many after a dramatic losing skid, but he silenced those doubters after regaining his bantamweight title last December
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Somewhat lost in the pageantry and historical relevance of Saturday's UFC bantamweight title trilogy in Abu Dhabi is the fact that two-time champion Petr Yan is in the midst of one of the greatest comeback arcs in recent memory. Yan (20-5), who regained the title from Merab Dvalishvili (21-5) last December in their rematch via upset decision, will be the betting favorite when the two meet for a third time in the co-main event of UFC 333 inside Etihad Arena. And the current standing of the pound-for-pound ranked native of Russia is a far cry from where the 33-year-old Yan was just a few years ago. In 2020, Yan was on top of the MMA world after stopping Brazilian legend Jose Aldo in the fifth round of their vacant 135-pound title bout. With a 15-1 record, a well-rounded game and an intimidating mean streak, Yan looked like the long-term future of the division. All of that would drastically change, of course, in his next fight when poor decision making led to him losing his title to Aljamain Sterling via disqualification for an illegal knee to a downed opponent in a fight he was winning. 
Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 333 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!Even though Yan responded by outpointing Cory Sandhagen just seven months later to claim the interim title at UFC 267, few could've predicted the immediate three-fight losing skid that followed, as just about everyone declared Yan as no longer being an elite threat. 
        
            
                Merab Dvalishvili looks to make history in trilogy bout with Petr Yan at UFC 333: 'Age is just a number'
                
                    Brian Campbell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The only one who didn't count Yan out, apparently, was the fighter himself. And beginning in 2024, he set course on a four-fight win streak that now has him back and seemingly better than ever.
"It's just something that you want to say to all of the people in the world, anybody who doubts themselves or anyone who says maybe I can't accomplish it or maybe I can't achieve it anymore," Yan told CBS Sports on Tuesday, through an interpreter. "It's not to doubt yourself but to keep doing what they do and keep moving forward and keep believing in themselves."Not all losing streaks are the same, and in hindsight, Yan's falloff was just as much about stubbornness and disputed decisions against elite opponents as anything else.Yan began his losing skid with consecutive split decisions against Sterling (in their title rematch) and future champion Sean O'Malley. And the third straight defeat, against Dvalishvili in their first meeting in 2023, was a fight in which Yan was severely hampered by a pre-existing broken right hand. 
"If you go back, my manager wanted to take me off the fight. He wanted to say no but I said, 'Absolutely not. We are going forward with it,'" Yan said. "If you look at the five rounds of the fight, I think I threw my right hand maybe twice. It was basically a non-working hand that I came out there with. This was something that we carried on through and something that we overcame. You saw the difference in the second fight and now is the time to put a big, fat exclamation point on this thing."In the first fight, Yan was taken down 11 times as Dvalishvili, who was in the midst of an incredible 14-fight win streak that would see him become champion, set a UFC record with 49 takedowns attempted. But everything changed two years later when a healthy Yan quickly reset the terms of their rematch at UFC 323.Not only did Yan get up quickly from the only two takedowns secured by Dvalishvili, he was able to use his own offensive wrestling to take "The Machine" down five times, which is the highest amount surrendered by Dvalishvili in 17 UFC bouts. And after neutralizing the two most dangerous weapons in Dvalishvili's game – his cardio and his wrestling – Yan began to take it to him on the feet and had his opponent badly hurt in Round 3 thanks to a pair of liver kicks.
"Obviously, [Dvalishvili] had that huge winning streak, but I think that everyone is beatable," Yan said. "He was basically a tanker truck before and I brought him back to being human."The one thing Yan doesn't hold on to is regret as he enters a fight in which the winner would have a strong claim for consideration as the best and most accomplished bantamweight in UFC history. Asked whether he would go back and change the result of the Sterling disqualification loss in 2020 if he could, Yan leaned upon the wisdom he has acquired throughout this journey. 
"I think it was important to me to go through all of those trials and tribulations and all of that hard time," Yan said. "There's a proverb that we have, or a saying, where we can't change our past, but we can dictate how our future is going to go."
Yan will also get support on Saturday from an unlikely place in the form of his oldest child, his 10-year-old son Daniil, an aspiring martial artist himself, who will serve as a cornerman for the first time. Daniil first became known to UFC fans in 2024 when, after Yan defeated Deiveson Figueiredo in Macau, his son spoke during the postfight interview of how proud he was of his father, who had won his second straight fight following the losing skid. A smiling Daniil also interjected himself into his father's interview with CBS Sports this week, making sure to let it be known that he's predicting a knockout of Dvalishvili. "[My sons] are young sportsmen themselves right now," Yan said. "The oldest one is 10, and the youngest one is six. They are doing MMA and working on stuff. I think for a few years now, they have been watching my fights, so they fully understand what I do. They understand what this is all about and I think it's a great example I can set for them going forward."
Interestingly enough, Yan echoed his son's prediction of a finish on Saturday and said he will do so by knockout.  "I miss my vocation, I miss the fighting. I want to come out and put on a beautiful show," Yan said. "I want to show a master class of MMA on Saturday. I'm going to smash him."Who wins Volkanovski vs. Evloev, and how exactly does the fight end? Visit SportsLine now to get detailed picks and analysis from the incomparable expert who is up over $21,000 on his UFC picks since May 2018, and find out.
